## Routing verdict from the `domain:cli` seat — ⛔ NOT a transfer to `cloud`, and ⛔ not dispatchable as one card

`objectstack-ai/cloud` became readable to this seat today (2026-08-12), which finally allows the file-at-destination judgement this card has been waiting on since it was filed. I read it rather than dispatching, because the obvious answer turns out to be wrong.

**The obvious answer — "the control plane is `cloud`, so transfer it there" — is incorrect.** By the card's own table, most of this work lands in **this** repo:

| category | fields | lands in |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Dead** | `slug`, `project_type`, `region`, `is_system`, `clone_from_environment_id` | `packages/client` — **objectstack** (`domain:cli`) |
| **3. Policy-overridden** | `driver`, `plan`, `storage_limit_mb` | `packages/client` type + the `os env create --driver/--plan` flags in `packages/cli` — **objectstack** (`domain:cli`) |
| **2. Dialect-dropped** | `is_default`, `env_type` | **one end or the other** — see below |
| **4. Body-level guard** | — | **cloud** (the card says so: "that guard would have to live in `cloud`, like its sibling") |

Transferring the whole card to cloud would have moved the SDK trims and the CLI flags — the majority of the work — into a repo whose seat cannot land them.

### Why it is also not one dispatch

Category 2 is the only category where a user is **actively misled today** (`--default` and the env type are silently dropped on the wire), and it carries a real contract decision the card names but does not settle: **which spelling wins.** The handler already accepts snake_case for `display_name` and `organization_id` but camelCase-only for `isDefault` / `environmentType` — a third spelling, `environment_type`, appears too. Either the cloud handler accepts `is_default` / `env_type` (matching how it already treats its neighbours), or the SDK sends camelCase. Contract-first says one spelling wins, not both — but *which* end changes which repo lands the fix, and a wire-format decision made unilaterally by whichever seat happens to pick the card up first is how the two ends drift again.

So this is a **contract-first split** (multi-repo rule 2), not a transfer and not a single dispatch: a parent plus per-repo sub-issues, the contract half first, downstream halves carrying `Blocked-by:`.

### Handing it to the triage seat, because the split is theirs to make

Under rule 4 the splitting and ordering of a cross-repo parent/sub-issue chain belongs to the **triage seat**, not to an executor lane. I am not doing it here, and I am not dispatching the card as-is. What this comment adds is the measurement that makes the split cheap:

1. **Decide the category-2 spelling first** — it is the contract, and it determines whether that sub-issue is a `cloud` card or an `objectstack` card. Candidate for the decision box if the two ends are genuinely balanced; my read is that the handler accepting snake_case is the smaller, more consistent change (it already does so for two of its four fields), but this seat does not own the cloud wire format.
2. **Categories 1 + 3 are `objectstack` / `domain:cli`** and are safely dispatchable **independently** — they are SDK-type and CLI-flag trims with no cloud dependency. This lane can take them as soon as they exist as their own card. Category 3 additionally needs the trim-or-document call the card names ("do not leave a typed field the server discards"), and the CLI half is the sharper edge: `os env create --plan` even *defaults* to `free`, so users are offered a choice with no effect.
3. **Category 4 (the guard) is a `cloud` card**, and worth its own grading — the card is right that route-level guards are structurally blind here, since both existing audits compare **URLs**, and a body field the server never reads is invisible to them. That is the general lesson and it outlives these 13 fields.

⛔ Not claiming, not dispatching, not transferring. Leaving `pm:queue` + `domain:cli` in place so the triage seat sees it; ⛔ I have not changed the grade or the routing label, since a card that is about to be split should not be re-routed by the lane that is handing it over.

Related: #3702, #3731 (the sibling trims, same family), #3563 (the guard family), #5958 (the other cloud-blocked card in this lane, being read separately).

## This hold's `Restart-when:` is a reminder, not a predicate — and category 2 is a live defect

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024) · state audit of all 10 `pm:on-hold` cards in the lane, at the maintainer's instruction. State transition: `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue` (one `replace`).

### Why the hold was not legal

The body's first line reads:

> Restart-when: the triage seat performs the contract-first split (parent + per-repo sub-issues) — decide the category-2 wire spelling first …

⛔ That is not a condition on an external event; it is *"wait until a seat does the work"*. Nothing schedules it, so no mechanism can ever wake this card — the hold has been load-bearing on someone happening to re-read it, for 44 days. `pm:on-hold` requires a machine-readable `Restart-when:`, and a card with no wake mechanism must not be held at all.

⚠️ Note this is the *opposite* failure to #7898's, found in the same audit: there the predicate was well-formed and had already fired unswept; here the predicate cannot fire by construction. Both were invisible for the same reason — `Restart-when:` has no unlock sweep the way `Blocked-by:` does.

### Why it goes back to the queue rather than staying parked

⭐ The card's own words about category 2, unchanged since filing:

> **Dialect-dropped** (`is_default`, `env_type`) … This is the sharpest one: it is a **live** feature that quietly does nothing.

and

> Fix (2) — it is the only category where a user can be *actively misled today* (they pass `--default` / an env type and it vanishes).

A reproducible, user-reachable defect does not belong in a hold. `os env create --default` accepts the flag, the SDK serialises `is_default`, and the control-plane handler reads `Boolean(body.isDefault)` — camelCase only — so the flag is dropped on the wire with no error at either end.

### What is dispatchable from this lane, and what is not

⛔ Deliberately **not** doing the contract-first split from this seat — that is the triage seat's act, and category 2 selects a landing repo, which is above this seat's floor. Recording the shape so whoever picks it up does not re-derive it:

| category | fields | landing repo | dispatchable now? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — dead** | `slug`, `project_type`, `region`, `is_system`, `clone_from_environment_id` | `objectstack` (`packages/client`) | ✅ yes — pure `domain:cli`, same treatment as #3702 / #3731, changeset included |
| **2 — dialect-dropped** | `is_default`, `env_type` | ⚠️ **undecided** — either `cloud` (handler accepts snake_case, matching how it already treats `display_name` / `organization_id`) or `objectstack` (SDK sends camelCase) | ⛔ no — the wire spelling must be chosen first, and it selects the repo |
| **3 — policy-overridden** | `driver`, `plan`, `storage_limit_mb` | `objectstack` (`packages/client`) + CLI flag surface | ⚠️ needs a trim-or-document ruling first; the code half is then `domain:cli` |

⚠️ One flag for whoever takes category 2: ⛔ do **not** resolve it by making the handler accept *both* spellings. Prime Directive #12 forbids lenient dual-dialect fallback, and the body's own directive says "one spelling should win, not both". The handler already carries three spellings for `env_type` (`environmentType` / `environment_type` / the SDK's `env_type`); that is the disease, not the cure.

### ⛔ Not asserted here

- ⛔ No priority label produced by this seat.
- ⛔ No claim that categories 1 and 3 are urgent — they are trims and a documentation ruling, and can sit in the queue at whatever grade triage gives them.
- ⛔ The body-level guard question (item 4 of the card's suggested order) is untouched and remains the last item, informed by 1–3, exactly as filed.

## ⛔ Correction to my comment above

I wrote that this card and #7898 were *"invisible for the same reason — `Restart-when:` has no unlock sweep the way `Blocked-by:` does."* **That is false.** `Restart-when: closed <owner/repo>#N` is fired by the same unlock scan as `Blocked-by:` (both channels since #10403), and `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` carries **H9** (`:2047`) for hold exits and **H17** (`:3085`) for hold trigger files.

The accurate reason this card stayed invisible is narrower: H9's fireability test is

```js
directiveValues(text, 'Restart-when').some((v) => !/^manual\b/i.test(v))
```

⇒ **any value not beginning with `manual` passes.** "the triage seat performs the contract-first split" passes. H9 has been green on this card the whole time, because a line is there — it tests the *spelling* of fireability, not fireability.

⛔ The transition stands unchanged: `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue`, for the reasons given (nothing can fire this predicate, and category 2 is a live defect). Only my account of the machinery was wrong. Corrected analysis filed as **#17377**.
